text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyPrimates Also Become Germophobes After Living Through a Viral OutbreakAnd it could shed light on the evolutionary origins of disgustJCBy Jake Currie6:05 PM CDT on October 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleRemember the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic? Without having a solid handle on how the virus spread, we were left to quarantine our mail, wipe down any packages with disinfectant, and wash our produce with soap and water. According to a new study published in Royal Society Open Science, humans aren’t the only primates who take extreme precautions during viral outbreaks.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayIn 2020, a Texas primate sanctuary was dealing with its own mini-pandemic. Simian retrovirus Type II, a virus that causes an immune deficiency similar to AIDS in primates, swept through three of four groups of Japanese macaques housed at the sanctuary. Bad news for the monkeys, but good news for cognitive scientists from the University of California San Diego.
